entry.title: Coding Period Week 1
entry.content:
The first week of the coding period was focused on testing the Cityscapes dataset adapter I started during the community bonding period, improving its implementation based on feedback from my mentors, preparing the tutorial for Cityscapes image segmentation, and exploring the SemanticKITTI dataset to understand how to support it in PerceptionMetrics.

Improving the Cityscapes Adapter

This week, I continued working on the Cityscapes dataset adapter and updated it based on the feedback and merges from last week. The main goal was to make the adapter fit better with the existing PerceptionMetrics dataset interface and ensure that it can be used cleanly from the evaluation pipeline.

I worked on cleaning up the adapter implementation, registering the dataset so that it can be built through the common dataset creation workflow, and fixing the arguments passed through build_dataset. I also restored the required cityscapesscripts dependency, since the adapter uses the official Cityscapes label definitions to build the ontology and class mappings.

Another important part of the work was checking how the adapter handles Cityscapes train IDs and label IDs. This is important because many pretrained segmentation models use train IDs, while the original dataset also provides raw label IDs. Making this configurable should make the adapter easier to use with different evaluation setups.

Cityscapes Tutorial

I also completed preparing a dedicated Cityscapes image segmentation tutorial for PerceptionMetrics. The tutorial shows how to load the Cityscapes dataset, configure the ontology, use a pretrained segmentation model, and export the data in a format that can be evaluated by the existing metrics pipeline.

For this, I experimented with a pretrained SegFormer model fine-tuned on Cityscapes and checked how its predictions align with the ontology generated by the adapter. This helped me verify the adapter beyond just loading files, because the tutorial exercises the complete flow from dataset loading to prediction and evaluation preparation.

A screenshot of the tutorial is shown below, where you can see the predicted segmentation masks overlaid on the original Cityscapes images.

Exploring SemanticKITTI

In parallel, I started exploring the SemanticKITTI dataset to understand what will be needed for future support. Since SemanticKITTI is a LiDAR semantic segmentation dataset, it has a different structure from Cityscapes and requires working with point clouds, binary label files, and sequence-based organization.

I looked at the existing LiDAR utilities in PerceptionMetrics and compared them with the SemanticKITTI data format. This helped me identify which parts of the current codebase can already be reused and which parts will need a new dataset adapter or additional configuration.

David also suggested using the MMDetection3D codebase as the model zoo for SemanticKITTI, since it has many pretrained models and a well-established evaluation pipeline. The adapter will follow a structure similar to the usual LiDAR dataset adapters. This will involve loading the point cloud data, matching it with the corresponding label files, and building an ontology based on the SemanticKITTI class definitions.

The visualization of point clouds and predicted labels using VisPy looked very good, and David suggested comparing both Open3D and VisPy for this part. This will be important for the tutorial, since visualizing point clouds with predicted labels is a key part of understanding the results. David also suggested experimenting with the LiDAR utilities available in torch_segmentation.py.

Below is a screenshot of the beautiful visualizations of SemanticKITTI point clouds and labels using VisPy, which will be a great reference for the tutorial.

Next Steps

This week, David merged both the Cityscapes adapter and the tutorial, which is great progress. In the coming week, I plan to start working on the SemanticKITTI dataset adapter, focusing on loading point cloud data and matching it with the corresponding labels.

I also plan to experiment more with the existing LiDAR utilities, compare Open3D and VisPy for visualization, and start preparing the structure for a future SemanticKITTI tutorial.
entry.summary: Implementing the Cityscapes tutorial and improving the dataset adapter, exploring SemanticKITTI dataset

entry.title: Community Bonding Week 1
entry.content:
The second week of the GSoC community bonding period was focused on diving deeper into the PerceptionMetrics codebase, understanding how dataset adapters are implemented, and beginning to experiment with evaluation workflows. My main goal for the week was to understand the existing dataset structure in the project and start preparing the initial support for Cityscapes.

Exploring PerceptionMetrics

I spent time going through the evaluation pipeline in PerceptionMetrics to understand how datasets, ontologies, predictions, and labels are connected during evaluation. This helped me understand what information a dataset adapter needs to provide and how the data should be formatted before it can be used by the metrics module.

I also looked at the existing GOOSE dataset adapter as a reference. This was useful for understanding the expected structure of dataset dictionaries, ontology dictionaries, and how image-label pairs are collected before being passed to the segmentation dataset wrapper.

Starting the Cityscapes Adapter

I started integrating support for the Cityscapes dataset by writing an initial adapter for semantic segmentation. The adapter loads Cityscapes images and matches them with their corresponding ground-truth label files based on the standard Cityscapes folder structure.

This involved handling the train, validation, and test splits, building image and label paths, and creating an ontology from the official Cityscapes label definitions. I also worked on making the implementation configurable so that different image and label directories or suffixes can be passed if needed.

Community Meeting

This week, I also attended a group meeting with the JdeRobot team. During the meeting, we introduced ourselves, discussed the project methodology, and reviewed the expected timelines and outcomes for GSoC.

It was helpful to hear about the broader goals of the organization.

Next Steps

In the coming week, I plan to continue improving the Cityscapes dataset adapter and test it more thoroughly with the PerceptionMetrics evaluation pipeline. I will also refine the implementation based on feedback from my mentors, clean up the API where needed, and start checking how the adapter behaves with real Cityscapes samples.
entry.summary: Exploring PerceptionMetrics, Cityscapes, and evaluation workflows

entry.title: Community Bonding Week 0
entry.content:
The first week of the GSoC community bonding period has mainly been focused on getting everything set up and becoming more familiar with the project workflow and datasets.

Meeting the Mentors

This week, I had discussions with the mentors regarding the overall direction of the project, expectations for the coding period, and the planned milestones for the upcoming weeks.

Setting Up the Blog

I also spent some time setting up this blog using the al-folio Jekyll theme and GitHub Pages. Since this is my first time maintaining a project blog in this format, there was a bit of debugging involved with GitHub Actions, deployment configuration, and asset management.

The website is now live and will be used to document weekly progress throughout Google Summer of Code 2026.

Exploring the Cityscapes Dataset

Another major part of this week involved exploring the Cityscapes dataset and understanding how semantic segmentation annotations are organized.

I spent some time understanding:

  • Dataset directory structure
  • labelIds and trainIds
  • Semantic segmentation masks
  • Visualization pipelines
  • Mapping RGB images to corresponding annotations

I also began writing utilities for loading images and their corresponding segmentation labels, which will later help during integration into PerceptionMetrics.

Next Steps

For the next week, the plan is to:

  • Continue understanding the PerceptionMetrics codebase
  • Explore dataset adapter implementations
  • Begin integrating additional dataset support
  • Start experimenting with evaluation workflows and metrics
entry.summary: Setting up the blog, meeting mentors, and exploring Cityscapes
